subject: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme

messages.author: 6bbd1026ab8e57c7
messages.subject: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme
parts:
Also posted on StackExchange....

I am building a Shiny web app (eventually to be deployed using Shiny Server) and I downloaded the Ambrosia web app theme from wrapbootstrap (https://wrapbootstrap.com/theme/ambrosia-web-application-theme-WB06SM719) to style the page. The local prototype of the home page is implemented as follows:


library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(suppressDepencies("bootstrap"),
    tags$head(
        tags$meta(name="description",content=""),
        tags$meta(name="viewport",content="width=device-width"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet",href="assets/styles/css/ambrosiabootstrap.min.css"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet", href="assets/font-awesome/css/ambrosia-font-awesome.css"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet", href="assets/styles/css/ambrosiastyle.css"),
        tags$script(src="assets/js/jquery-1.8.0.min.js"),
        tags$script(src="$.noConflict(true);"),
        tags$script(src="assets/js/bootstrap.min.js")),

    tags$body(
        tags$div(class="navbar navbar-default navbar-fixed-top",role="navigation",
            tags$div(class="container", 
                 #Etc.
            )
        )
    )

server <- function(input,output) {}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Notice that the Shiny bootstrap theme is suppressed - without this step the UI does not render properly and dynamic elements such as dropdown menus do not function. This solution is fine when there are no Shiny HTML widgets required in the UI and the server function is empty (i.e. no R calculations are taking place; the web page is just a simple HTML page rendered via Shiny using the Ambrosia style). However, conflicts arise when I add Shiny widgets and calculations to the server function. For example:

library(shiny)
library(plotly)

ui <- tags$head(<same as before except Shiny bootstrap is not suppressed>)
    tags$body(            
       tags$div(class="navbar navbar-default navbar-fixed-top",role="navigation",
            tags$div(class="container", 
                 #Etc.
            )
        )
       tags$div(class="container",
           tags$div(class="row",
               tags$div(class="col-lg-8",
                   dataTableOutput("table"),
                   plotlyOutput("plot)",
               )
           )
       )
    )

server <- function(input,output) {

    x <- rnorm(50),
    y <- rnorm(50),
    dat <- data.table(x,y),
    names(dat) <- c("x","y"),

    output$table <- renderDataTable(dat),
    output$plot <- renderPlotly({
        datplot <- plot_ly(dat,x=x,y=y,title="Plot",shape=list(spline))
    })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

This scenario will correctly render the datatable and plotly graph, but the Ambrosia UI is messed up (text in wrong location, dynamic elements not functioning, etc.). If I restore the suppressDepencies("bootstrap") command, the UI is restored but none of the Shiny/plotly elements render. I have tried using a compiled Less CSS file to apply Ambrosia styling only to certain elements in the UI without success. Any ideas on how to resolve this conflict?


For reference, Shiny loads the following command in the tags$head() section when bootstrap is not suppressed:


<script type="application/html-dependencies">json2[2014.02.04];jquery[1.11.3];shiny[0.13.2];**bootstrap[9999]**;datatables[1.10.5];datatables-bootstrap[1.10.5];htmlwidgets[0.6];plotlyjs[1.6.1];plotly-binding[3.4.1]</script><script src="shared/json2-min.js"></script>


When suppressed, it looks like this:


<script type="application/html-dependencies">json2[2014.02.04];jquery[1.11.3];shiny[0.13.2];datatables[1.10.5];datatables-bootstrap[1.10.5];htmlwidgets[0.6];plotlyjs[1.6.1];plotly-binding[3.4.1];bootstrap[3.3.5]</script><script src="shared/json2-min.js"></script>
